questions.title: What happens if you lose your ball or hit it out of bounds?
questions.question: You hit a ball and think it might be lost or out of bounds, so you play another ball as a provisional. Later, you can't find your first ball or you see it's out of bounds. What should you do next?

choices.text: Now the provisional ball is your ball to play, and you add one extra shot.
You get to hit again from where you last played, with no extra shots.
You can pick which ball you want to use, with no extra shots.
You must drop a new ball where your first ball went out, and add two extra shots.

questions.explanation: If your first ball is lost or out of bounds, the provisional ball you played becomes your ball. You must add one extra shot to your score.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: An extra ball you play just in case your first ball is lost or out of bounds.
A place off the golf course where you are not allowed to play your ball from.

questions.teachingTip: Show the boundary on a hole and let kids practise saying 'provisional ball' when they think their shot might be lost or out of bounds.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids may think they can choose the better ball to use.
They may forget to add the penalty shot.
They may try to drop a ball where the first ball went out instead of playing the provisional.

questions.title: What if your original ball is out of bounds or not found?
questions.question: You play a provisional ball. Your original ball is later found to be out of bounds, or you don't find it within 3 minutes. What should you do next?

choices.text: The provisional ball becomes your ball in play, with a 1-stroke penalty
You must replay your shot from the previous spot with no penalty
You can choose to play either ball with no penalty
You must drop a new ball where the original went out of bounds, with a 2-stroke penalty

questions.explanation: If your original ball is out of bounds or lost (not found within 3 minutes), the provisional ball becomes the ball in play and you count a one-stroke penalty.
